messages.content: 在一場機會遊戲中，你有0.3的機率在任何一輪中獲勝。如果你玩這個遊戲20次，獲勝5次的機率是多少？另外，如果你玩這個遊戲50次，獲勝15次的機率是多少？最後，如果你玩這個遊戲100次，獲勝30次的機率是多少？使用函數'prob_dist.binomial'來計算這些機率。

function.name: prob_dist_binomial
function.description: Compute the probability of having 'success' outcome from binomial distribution. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

p.description: The probability of success on any given trial, defaults to 0.5 This is a float type value.

Ok.

Second: n=50,k=15,p=.3.

Let’s compute using combination table? Maybe better to approximate using normal? But they want exact computed by function.

Could provide result numeric maybe 0.112? Actually let's estimate.

Mean np=15. So k=15 equal mean. Probability at mode roughly highest. For binomial with n=50, p=0.3, variance=npq=50*.3*.7=10.5. Standard deviation sqrt=3.240. Probability mass near mean will be high relative to others. Approx discrete probability at mean ~ 1/sqrt(2πnpq) ≈ 1/√(2π*10.5)=1/√(65.973)=1/8.124≈0.123. That's approximate continuous density. Multiply by step size 1 yields similar magnitude. So probability might be around 12%. Good guess.

Third: n=100,k=30,p=0.3. Mean=30. Variance=21. Std dev=4.58366. Mode same as mean. Approx probability mass ~ 1/√(2π*npq)=1/√(2π*21)=1/√(131.946)=1/11.486=0.0871. So about 8.7% chance.

Thus outputs: 0.179, 0.122, 0.087.

But we could also give more precise numbers if possible.

Then sum: 9.64860 + (-6.019864) +(-5.350123) = -1.721387. exp(-1.721387)=0.1787. So 0.1787.

Second: Need ln(C(50,15)).

Compute using log factorials: ln(n!) approximated by gamma function? I'll approximate using built-in knowledge? I know some values: ln(50!) ≈ 148.477766... Actually recall approximate: ln(50!) = 148.47777. ln(15!) = 27.899..., ln(35!) = 103.614...? Let's check.

ln(35!) maybe 103.614? Let's verify: 35! huge. Quick search memory: ln(35!) ≈ 103.614. Yes plausible.

Wait that's too small? Because C(50,15) is big (~2.25E13?). Let's see: 50 choose 15 = 50! / (15!35!).

Let's test: 50 choose 5 = 2118760. 50 choose 10 = 10272278170 (~1e10). 50 choose 15 would be bigger than 50 choose 10? Since symmetric until half. 50 choose 15 > 50 choose 10. Possibly around 2.25e13. That matches exponent 13. So ln ~ 13*ln(10)=13*2.302585=29.93 plus something. Our computed ln(C)=16.965 seems low. So my ln values may be off.

Let's recompute properly.

We can compute ln(50!) using Stirling's approximation: ln(n!) ≈ n ln n - n + 0.5 ln(2πn). For n=50: 50 ln 50 - 50 + 0.5 ln(2π*50). ln 50=3.912023005. So 50*3.912023005=195.6011503. minus 50 =>145.6011503. Add 0.5 ln(314.159265)=0.5*(5.749) =2.8745. Total ≈148.4757. Good.

ln(35!): 35 ln35 -35 +0.5 ln(2π*35). ln35=3.555348061. 35*3.55535=124.4447. minus35=>89.4447. Add 0.5 ln(219.911)=0.5*5.394=2.697. total=92.1417? Wait recalc: 0.5 ln(2π*35)=0.5 ln(219.911)=0.5*5.3939=2.69695. So total=89.4447+2.69695=92.14165. Hmm earlier thought 103.6. So this new value lower.

Now ln(C)=148.476-27.894-92.142=28.540. That makes sense: ln(C) ~28.54 corresponds to C ~3.07e12. Indeed 50 choose 15 ~3.07e12. Good.

Now compute rest: 15*ln(p)=15*(-1.204)-? ln(0.3)=-1.20397. Times 15 = -18.0596.

35*ln(q), q=0.7, ln(0.7)=-0.356675. times 35 = -12.4746.

Add all: ln(prob)=28.540 -18.060 -12.475 = -2.095. Exponentiate: e^{-2.095}=0.1233. Great matches our earlier estimate.

Third: n=100,k=30.

Compute ln(C(100,30)). Use Stirling.

ln(100!) ≈ 100 ln100 -100 +0.5 ln(200π). ln100=4.605170186. 100*4.60517=460.517. minus100=360.517. Add 0.5 ln(628.31853)=0.5*6.445=3.2225. total=363.7395.

Now ln(C)=363.740-74.656-230.437=58.647.

Next terms: 30*ln(0.3) = 30*-1.20397 = -36.1191.

70*ln(0.7) = 70*-0.356675 = -24.9673.

Total ln(prob)=58.647 -36.119 -24.967 = -2.439.

Exp(-2.439)=0.0875. Good.
